item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I really wanted to give this an upvote, but the recovery team being full of morons is forcing me to downvote.

It should have been loaded into the trailer of a semi or something, not driven by the recovery team. Also, people disappeared, they found human ice cream, and somehow knew it was anomalous? The only thing those individual facts point to is a serial killer. They would have needed to observe an "activation" in order to know it should be a scip, and then the recovery team dying wouldn't have been a thing because they'd know what it does at that point.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
If there are multiple subjects affected then each will line up and wait for the doors to open again, or until the 3-hour window has elapsed. Subjects outside the vehicle when time elapses will wander away in apparent confusion; when interviewed, they appear to have no memory of the event. After 5 AM the SCP will lose its abnormal ability and the back doors can be opened. Any person(s) that entered into the truck during the time that the music was playing will vanish.

Discovering the truck and its contents the team paid the fine for it and drove it to Site-17. During the trip it activated, causing the death of all team members except for Agent ██████, who was driving the team's vehicle and realized what was causing his teammates to become entranced.

I feel like there is some conflisting action going on just for the sake of death and blood. Why would the team drive the ice cream van cross country, and why would all the teams but one go missing before they realized it was having an affect on people? What? The guy driving is stopping every three hours and not wondering what his teammates are doing lining up for "blood ice cream"?

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I looked over it again. I like that you got rid of the dinky little note. Good work!

But now that I look at what you mean by 'self aware', I find this very cartoony. I'd prefer if it was just sitting there and playing the music and getting the people, not freaking out on people. That, my friend, is the fine line between 'Oh my god this is terrifying I'm getting out of this state' and 'Oh hey, it's Scooby Doo time.'

It is also the fine line between my upvote and downvote. Keep trying, though. If you make it less Scooby Doo and more serious, I'll change my vote.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Overall, I like this concept. Not exactly a new idea, and not terribly memorable, but cool and creepy all the same. A few things:

I'm not a fan of that bit at the end about how it started ramming into vehicles when boxed in, especially since it apparently perfectly content to sit around because of a parking boot. I think I prefer the idea of this simply being a machine doing what it was built to when able, not some malevolent force of destruction.

This is a bit long. You go into heavy detail with both recovery and, more problematic, why it isn't special. When reading an SCP, I assume that it is completely normal until you tell me otherwise; you don't need to spend a paragraph describing how everything operates completely normally. You could cut out pretty much the second half of that paragraph and it would work just fine. That being said, if it uses a standard diesel engine, where does it get fuel?

Also, you really need to fix the formatting on the second photo.

So yeah, there's my two cents.

item.content:encoded:
Yeah, it does need some work. I'd do it myself, but it's late.

As it stands now, I do not like the note at the end noting that the thing is self aware. There's no more information on that. No experimentation, no results, no nothing. You don't just throw those things in. You need information on how and why it is self aware.

Personally, ice cream trucks scare me, and it being from Massachusetts doesn't help. … we make a shitton of freaky things, lemme tell you. The effects of the truck itself are creepy enough as it is. You don't need to throw stuff in like that.

Over all, get rid of that little note and do some hardcore proofreading. Commas are followed by spaces always, and never should a comma follow a space. Commas are ladies and children. Spaces are men. Women and children first, my love.
